::: {.lead}
*Byte Bay* will soon release *Neon Drift*. Players write to the studio
before they buy: "Will it run on my laptop?" "My phone says it is not
compatible. Why?" To answer, a developer puts two lists side by side: the
**system requirements** of the game and the **specification sheet** of the
device. In lecture 4 you read spec sheets. In lecture 5 you met the GPU and
the graphics settings. In this lesson you compare specifications line by
line, decide if a game runs, and find the part that holds it back. Every
section ends with a short task.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary system-requirements specifications compatibility bottleneck graphics-settings video-memory storage-capacity operating-system >}}

## 6.1 What does the game need? System requirements

Every store page of a game lists what a device needs. These are the
**system requirements**. For PC games, there are usually two columns
(@fig-req):

- **Minimum:** the game starts and runs, but at low settings.
- **Recommended:** the game runs well at normal settings.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 6.1 — System requirements"}
The **system requirements** of a game list the specifications that a device
needs. The **minimum** requirements let it run at low settings. The
**recommended** requirements let it run well.
:::

![The system requirements of Neon Drift for PC.](images/requirements.png){#fig-req width=94%}

Phone stores show less. Google Play shows "Requires Android" (the oldest
Android version) and the download size. The App Store shows "Compatibility"
(for example "Requires iOS 15.0 or later") and the size. Studios often
write more in the game's description, such as the RAM.

::: {.callout-note title="Example 6.1 — Reading the requirements of Neon Drift"}
Look at @fig-req.

1. A PC with 8 GB of RAM meets the minimum, but not the recommended 16 GB.
2. A graphics card is recommended. An integrated GPU with 2 GB is enough for
   the minimum only.
3. Both columns need 20 GB of free storage. The recommended column wants an
   SSD, so that levels load fast (lecture 3).
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Reading "minimum" as "good enough". At the minimum, the game runs at low
settings. Many players are not happy with it. A studio that tests only on
minimum devices does not see how most players will play.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find the requirements of a game"}
On your phone, open the store page of a game that you play.

- **Android (Google Play):** tap **About this game** and find **Requires
  Android**.
- **iPhone (App Store):** scroll to **Information** and find **Size** and
  **Compatibility**.

*Your result:* the name of the game, the OS version it requires and its
size.
:::

## 6.2 Does it run here? Comparing line by line

A player asks: "Will Neon Drift run on my laptop?" The developer compares
each line of the requirements with the same line of the spec sheet. Each
line gets a result: below minimum, minimum or recommended. Then one rule
decides: **the weakest line decides** the level of the whole device
(@fig-compare).

![Laptop L1 against the requirements: the graphics line is only at the minimum.](images/compare-lines.png){#fig-compare width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 6.2 — Laptop L1"}
Laptop L1 (lecture 4): Windows 11; 8 cores, up to 4.4 GHz; 16 GB RAM; GPU
inside the processor with 2 GB; 512 GB SSD with 120 GB free.

1. OS, processor, memory and storage reach the recommended column.
2. Graphics: 2 GB, integrated. That meets the minimum (2 GB), but the
   recommended column needs a graphics card with 6 GB.
3. The weakest line is the graphics line, so L1 reaches only the
   **minimum**. Neon Drift runs on L1 at low settings.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Example 6.3 — The old PC"}
Old PC O1: Windows 10 (64-bit); 4 cores, 3.0 GHz; 4 GB RAM; graphics card
with 2 GB; 60 GB free on a hard disk (HDD).

1. OS, processor, graphics and storage meet the minimum.
2. Memory: 4 GB, but the minimum is 8 GB. This line is **below minimum**.
3. So O1 is below the minimum. The game may start, but it runs very badly.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Looking only at the strongest line: "8 cores at 4.4 GHz, so it runs well."
A fast processor does not help when the GPU is weak. The device is only as
good as its weakest line.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/spec-check.html" poster="sims/spec-check.png" title="Spec Check: does Neon Drift run here?" height="700" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Spec Check with the lab computer"}
Open the **Spec Check** simulator above (or scan its QR code). Use the spec
sheet of the lab computer from lecture 4 (or open **Settings → System →
About** and **Task Manager → Performance** again).

1. Choose **My lab computer** and enter its values.
2. Read the result of each line and the verdict.

*Your result:* the level of the lab computer and its weakest line.
:::

## 6.3 What holds the game back?

When a game does not run well, there are two different kinds of problem
(@fig-problems).

**A compatibility problem:** the game cannot be installed or started at
all. The OS version is too old, or there is not enough free storage. More
power does not help. The player must update the OS, free space, or use
another device.

**A performance problem:** the game runs, but slowly. One part is weaker
than the others: the **bottleneck**. The bottleneck decides the speed of the
whole device, like the narrow neck of a bottle.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 6.2 — Bottleneck"}
The **bottleneck** is the weakest part of a system. It limits the speed of
the whole system.
:::

![Two kinds of problems. On the right, the GPU is the bottleneck.](images/two-problems.png){#fig-problems width=94%}

Each bottleneck has its own fix (@tbl-fix). Lowering a setting moves work
away from the weak part.

| Bottleneck | What the player sees | What helps |
|---|---|---|
| GPU | low frame rate, more at high resolution | lower the resolution, shadows and effects |
| video memory | stutters with high textures | lower the texture quality |
| RAM | stops or freezes, "out of memory" | close other apps, lower the textures |
| CPU | slow with many cars or players | fewer objects; settings help little |
| storage | slow loading (HDD), or no install (full) | an SSD; free space |

: Bottlenecks and what helps. {#tbl-fix}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 6.4 — Three test phones"}
*Neon Drift Mobile* needs at least Android 10, 4 cores, 4 GB RAM and 4 GB of
free storage. It recommends Android 12, 8 cores and 6 GB RAM.

1. Phone P1 (Android 14, 8 cores, 8 GB RAM, 40 GB free): **recommended**.
2. Phone P3 (Android 9, 8 cores, 6 GB RAM, 30 GB free): Android 9 is too old.
   A **compatibility problem**: the store does not let the player install the game.
3. Phone P4 (Android 13, 8 cores, 4 GB RAM, 25 GB free): only the RAM is at
   the minimum. The game runs, at lower settings. The bottleneck is the RAM.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
"The phone has a fast chip, so the game must install." A fast chip does not
help with a compatibility problem. Android 9 cannot install a game that
needs Android 10, however fast the phone is.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Can your phone run it?"}
Use your phone's spec sheet from lecture 4 and the game requirements from
the Do it of section 6.1.

1. Compare the OS version and the free storage with the requirements.
2. Is there a compatibility problem? If the game runs slowly on your phone,
   which part is the bottleneck, and which setting would you lower?

*Your result:* two comparisons and your answer in one or two sentences.
:::

## Case study: test devices for Neon Drift

*Byte Bay* must choose its test devices for *Neon Drift*. For the PC version
(@fig-req) it has three computers:

- **Laptop L1:** Windows 11; 8 cores, up to 4.4 GHz; 16 GB RAM; GPU inside
  the processor, 2 GB; 120 GB free, SSD.
- **Desktop D1:** Windows 11; 6 cores, up to 4.0 GHz; 16 GB RAM; graphics
  card, 8 GB; 300 GB free, SSD.
- **Old PC O1:** Windows 10 (64-bit); 4 cores, 3.0 GHz; 4 GB RAM; graphics
  card, 2 GB; 60 GB free, HDD.

A good test lab has one device for each level: recommended, minimum, and
one below the minimum, to check the warning messages of the game. The Game
challenge of the interactive lesson uses these devices. In the mini-game
below you sort them, and three phones for the mobile version.

## Further reading

Tanenbaum and Austin, *Structured Computer Organization*, 6th ed., Chapter 2
(computer system organization and performance). The official Android
Developers and Apple Developer documentation on device compatibility.

## Exercises

1. What is the difference between the minimum and the recommended
   requirements?
2. Where does Google Play show the Android version that a game needs?
3. A game needs 8 GB RAM (minimum) and 16 GB (recommended). A laptop has
   12 GB. Which level does its memory line reach?
4. A PC reaches the recommended value on four lines and the minimum on one.
   Which level does it reach? Why?
5. Desktop D1 has 6 cores at up to 4.0 GHz, 16 GB RAM, a graphics card with
   8 GB and 300 GB free on an SSD. Which level does it reach for *Neon
   Drift*?
6. What is a bottleneck?
7. A phone has Android 9. A game needs Android 10. Is this a compatibility
   problem or a performance problem? What can the player do?
8. A game runs at 25 fps on a laptop with a weak integrated GPU. Which two
   settings should the player lower first?
9. *Byte Bay*: which computer is below the minimum, and which line is the
   reason?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Minimum: the game starts and runs at low settings. Recommended: it runs well at normal settings.
2. In About this game, the line Requires Android.
3. The minimum (12 GB is at least 8 GB, but less than 16 GB).
4. The minimum: the weakest line decides.
5. Recommended: every line reaches the recommended value.
6. The weakest part of a system; it limits the speed of the whole system.
7. A compatibility problem: the game cannot be installed. The player must update Android (if the phone allows it) or use another device.
8. The resolution and the shadows (or effects).
9. Old PC O1: its 4 GB of RAM is below the minimum of 8 GB.
:::
